Quantum random access code (n⟶m qubits)

Words: 157 Articles: 1
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
An encoding stores n classical bits in m qubits so that a receiver who later chooses a bit index can recover that bit with a specified success probability. The sender cannot tailor the encoding to the unknown requested index. This task permits approximate recovery of any one bit rather than simultaneous recovery of all bits, and must specify whether additional communication, shared randomness, or entanglement is allowed.

Optimal three-to-one qubit random access code (p∗​=21​(1+1/3​))

Words: 92
Quantum random access code OurBigBook.com
Encode signs sj​=(−1)bj​ by the unit Bloch vector (s1​,s2​,s3​)/3​. Perform the requested Pauli measurement and interpret a positive outcome as zero. Every input and index has success p∗​. To prove optimality, write each binary-measurement difference as Dj​=tj​I+vj​⋅σ, where positivity gives ∣vj​∣≤1−∣tj​∣. Averaging over all eight inputs cancels the tj​ terms. For any encoding vectors of norm at most one, the average success is at most 1/2+(1/48)∑s​∣∑j​sj​vj​∣. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality bounds the sum by 8∑j​∣vj​∣2​≤83​, proving the optimum even for mixed encodings and general binary measurements. The constant-success construction also maximizes worst-case success.

Classical communication

Words: 43
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
Classical communication transmits a distinguishable classical record, such as measurement bits, between parties. In quantum teleportation it tells the receiver which local correction to apply. Quantum no-signalling prevents shared entanglement alone from transmitting the record. A classical message cannot propagate across a spacelike separation in a relativistic protocol.

Remote state preparation

Words: 356 Articles: 5
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
Remote state preparation uses a shared entangled state, local measurement in quantum measurements and classical communication to prepare a state known to the sender at the receiver. The sender can tailor the measurement to the desired state, so restricted state families can require less communication than quantum teleportation. A real great-circle family of qubit states admits one-bit remote preparation of real qubit states.

Asymptotic remote state preparation by block indexing (EL/n⟶1)

Words: 71
Remote state preparation OurBigBook.com
Prepare independent candidate blocks by one-bit heralding of a remote state preparation block, but send only the first successful block's index. Success eventually occurs with probability one; a prefix code for a rare geometric success uses at most n+e/(e−1) expected bits per block. The expected singlet state consumption is n2n. Alternatively, limiting the number of trials to n2n gives failure probability at most e−n and a fixed message length n+log2​n+O(1). Both versions approach one classical bit per remotely prepared qubit in their respective expected-length or high-success senses.

Heralded remote preparation of an arbitrary qubit (psuccess​=1/2)

Words: 111 Articles: 1
Remote state preparation OurBigBook.com
For a target pure state ∣ψ⟩ of a qubit, choose its orthogonal complement so that
∣Ψ−⟩=2​∣ψ⟩∣ψ⊥⟩−∣ψ⊥⟩∣ψ⟩​.
(1)
Measuring the sender's half of this singlet state in that basis leaves the receiver in ∣ψ⟩ when the sender obtains ∣ψ⊥⟩. The outcome has probability one half. One classical success flag heralds the exact preparation without conveying the target's classical description.
// Target: quantum-theory.bigb

One-bit heralding of a remote state preparation block (psuccess​=2−n)

Words: 55
Heralded remote preparation of an arbitrary qubit OurBigBook.com
Apply heralded remote preparation of an arbitrary qubit independently to n shared singlet states. The sender reports one bit indicating whether every local outcome was successful. A positive flag certifies that the receiver's block is the desired product of n pure states; its probability is 2−n. A negative flag need not identify which states failed, since the whole block can be discarded.
// Target: algebra.bigb

Two-bit remote state preparation on a graph-state path

Words: 76
Remote state preparation OurBigBook.com
Alice holds the first two qubits and Bob the third of a three-vertex graph-state wire. Alice measures at α and (−1)rβ, with outcomes r,s, and sends these two bits. Bob applies ZrXs, the inverse of the known Pauli frame XsZr, obtaining U(β)U(α)∣+⟩ up to global phase. Bob need not know the angles. Every branch succeeds, with branch probability 1/4, and no postselection is needed. Alice's measurements and Bob's corrections constitute local operations and classical communication on the previously shared entangled resource.

One-bit remote preparation of real qubit states (iY∣βθ​⟩=∣αθ​⟩)

Words: 48
Remote state preparation OurBigBook.com
For ∣αθ​⟩=cosθ∣0⟩+sinθ∣1⟩, Alice measures her half of a Bell state in the real basis {∣αθ​⟩,∣βθ​⟩}, with ∣βθ​⟩=−sinθ∣0⟩+cosθ∣1⟩. Bob receives one outcome bit and applies I or iY. Since iY∣βθ​⟩=∣αθ​⟩ for every θ, the preparation is exact and the correction is independent of the unknown parameter.

Schumacher compression

Words: 489 Articles: 7
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
Schumacher compression is quantum source coding into the typical subspace of ρ⊗n. Asymptotically reliable compression is possible at every qubit rate above the Von Neumann entropy S(ρ).

Memoryless quantum information source (ρ=∑x​px​∣ψx​⟩⟨ψx​∣,ρ(n)=ρ⊗n)

Words: 74
Schumacher compression OurBigBook.com
A pure-state source emits independent states from a fixed quantum state ensemble. Its average block density operator is the tensor power of the one-use average. Unassisted reliable quantum source compression preserves the emitted quantum states, rather than only their classical labels. Schumacher compression gives the optimum asymptotic qubit rate S(ρ) for such a source, with every larger rate achievable. Nonorthogonal equally likely pure states need not have entropy one: their classical labels have entropy one but their average density operator can have lower Von Neumann entropy.

Quantum typical subspace (Tε(n)​)

Words: 129 Articles: 1
Schumacher compression OurBigBook.com
For a density operator π=∑i​qi​∣ϕi​⟩⟨ϕi​∣, the quantum typical subspace is spanned by product eigenvectors of π⊗n whose eigenvalues qi1​​⋯qin​​ satisfy
​−n1​log2​(qi1​​⋯qin​​)−S(π)​≤ε.
(2)
It applies the classical weakly typical sequence definition to the spectrum. If Pε(n)​ is its orthogonal projection, then
dimTε(n)​≤2n(S(π)+ε),Tr(π⊗nPε(n)​)⟶1.
(3)
The first statement follows from the typical-set cardinality bounds, and the second from the weak law of large numbers. This subspace holds nearly all the source probability while using exponentially fewer dimensions than the whole space when S(π)<log2​d.

Typical subspace theorem (Tr(π⊗nΠn,δ​)→1)

Words: 55
Quantum typical subspace OurBigBook.com
For each fixed δ>0, the quantum typical subspace projector selects eigenvalues of π⊗n between 2−n(S(π)+δ) and 2−n(S(π)−δ). Its probability tends to one by the weak law of large numbers for the spectral information variable. If its probability is at least 1−ϵ, its dimension is between (1−ϵ)2n(S(π)−δ) and 2n(S(π)+δ). These statements give the size and concentration estimates behind Schumacher compression.

Reliable quantum source compression

Words: 259 Articles: 3
Schumacher compression OurBigBook.com
A quantum source-compression scheme has encoding and decoding quantum channels with compressed space Kn​ and rate limsupn​n−1log2​dimKn​. For a pure-state source ensemble, average reliability means that the mean squared quantum fidelity after decoding tends to one. A stronger coherent criterion is Fe​(π⊗n,Dn​∘En​)→1, where entanglement fidelity also tests a purification reference. Encoding the quantum typical subspace achieves both criteria above S(π). Schumacher's original quantum coding paper establishes quantum source coding.

Typical-subspace compression with a failure flag (Fe​(π⊗n,Nn​)≥[Tr(π⊗nΠ)]2)

Words: 139 Articles: 1
Reliable quantum source compression OurBigBook.com
Measure the quantum typical subspace projector Π. Encode its successful sector isometrically and reserve one orthogonal compressed flag for failure; decode the flag to a fixed state. The composite channel is Nn​(τ)=ΠτΠ+Tr[(I−Π)τ]∣φ0​⟩⟨φ0​∣. It is trace preserving. The Kraus formula for entanglement fidelity gives the displayed lower bound, while convexity of the square gives the same bound for average pure-source fidelity. One flag adds only a vanishing asymptotic rate overhead.
Average pure-source fidelity after typical projection (F≥∑k​pk​αk4​≥2Tr(ρP)−1)
Words: 75
Typical-subspace compression with a failure flag OurBigBook.com
For a quantum state ensemble of pure vectors and an orthogonal projection P, measure {P,I−P}, preserve the successful subspace, and decode failure to a fixed normalized vector φ. The resulting quantum channel is Λ(X)=PXP+Tr[(I−P)X]∣φ⟩⟨φ∣. For αk​=∥Pψk​∥, its squared quantum fidelity on the kth source vector is αk4​+(1−αk2​)∣⟨ψk​∣φ⟩∣2. The inequality a2≥2a−1 on [0,1] proves the displayed average bound. It depends only on the source density operator's weight in P and does not require the emitted vectors to be orthogonal.

Finite-dimensional quantum compression converse (Fe​(ρ,DC)≤∑j<k​λj​)

Words: 51
Reliable quantum source compression OurBigBook.com
If encoding and decoding quantum channels factor through a k-dimensional space, their composite Kraus operators all have matrix rank at most k. The rank bound for a weighted operator trace and the Kraus formula for entanglement fidelity imply
Fe​(ρ,DC)≤∑j<k​λj​(ρ).
(4)
Thus high operation fidelity requires the leading k eigenvalues of the source density operator to carry almost all its probability. The bound applies to arbitrary completely positive trace-preserving encoders and decoders.

Classical-quantum state (CQ state)

Words: 190 Articles: 5
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
A classical-quantum state has block-diagonal form ρXB​=∑x​px​∣x⟩⟨x∣⊗ρx​. Its entropy is H(p)+∑x​px​S(ρx​).

Entropy of a classical-quantum state (S(∑x​px​∣x⟩⟨x∣⊗ρx​)=H(p)+∑x​px​S(ρx​))

Words: 40
Classical-quantum state OurBigBook.com
The classical-quantum state is block diagonal. If λxj​ are the eigenvalues of ρx​, its eigenvalues are px​λxj​. Inserting these into the definition of Von Neumann entropy gives the displayed sum of classical Shannon entropy and mean conditional quantum entropy. Its quantum mutual information is therefore the Holevo quantity S(∑x​px​ρx​)−∑x​px​S(ρx​).

Holevo quantity (χ)

Words: 136 Articles: 3
Classical-quantum state OurBigBook.com
For an ensemble {px​,ρx​} with average ρˉ​, the Holevo quantity is χ=S(ρˉ​)−∑x​px​S(ρx​)=I(X:B) of the associated classical-quantum state.

Holevo quantity under a quantum channel (χ({px​,Λ(ρx​)})≤χ({px​,ρx​}))

Words: 40
Holevo quantity OurBigBook.com
Attach an orthogonal classical label register to an ensemble. Its quantum mutual information with the quantum system equals the ensemble Holevo quantity. A local quantum channel changes the ensemble states but preserves their labels and probabilities. Data processing for quantum mutual information then proves that the output Holevo quantity cannot exceed the input value.

Holevo's theorem

Words: 79 Articles: 1
Holevo quantity OurBigBook.com
The classical mutual information obtained by any measurement of a quantum ensemble is at most its Holevo quantity. This follows from the data-processing inequality for quantum relative entropy applied to the measurement channel.
One-shot classical-quantum coding converse ((1−ϵ)log2​k≤I(X:Q)+1)
Words: 53
Holevo's theorem OurBigBook.com
For k equiprobable quantum code states with average decoding error ϵ<1, data-processing inequality for quantum relative entropy applied to the binary test for quantum decoding success gives
I(X:Q)≥(1−ϵ)log2​k−h2​(ϵ)−ϵlog2​(1−1/k)≥(1−ϵ)log2​k−1
(5)
for k≥2. Here h2​ is binary entropy. The case k=1 is trivial. Taking the supremum over allowed input distributions yields a code-size bound in terms of the largest Holevo quantity; at ϵ=1 the undivided inequality is vacuous.

Measure-and-prepare channel

Words: 110 Articles: 2
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
A measure-and-prepare channel measures a POVM {Mx​} and outputs a prescribed state σx​: T(ρ)=∑x​Tr(Mx​ρ)σx​. Such channels are exactly the entanglement-breaking channels.

Measurement channel

Words: 88 Articles: 1
Measure-and-prepare channel OurBigBook.com
A measurement channel writes a POVM's outcome into an orthogonal classical register:
Φ(X)=∑a​Tr(Ea​X)∣a⟩⟨a∣.
(6)
For any input orthonormal basis ∣j⟩, the Kraus operators Ka,j​=∣a⟩⟨j∣Ea​​ realize this map and satisfy ∑a,j​Ka,j†​Ka,j​=I. It is therefore a trace-preserving completely positive map.

Conditional input ensemble after a local measurement (ρCx,y​)

Words: 52
Measurement channel OurBigBook.com
For a bipartite input density operator ρACx​ and a POVM {Ey​} on A, let q(y∣x)=Tr[(Ey​⊗I)ρx]. For q(y∣x)>0, the conditioned input on C is
ρCx,y​=q(y∣x)TrA​[(Ey​​⊗I)ρx(Ey​​⊗I)]​.
(7)
Its positivity follows from the positive sandwich before the partial trace. A quantum channel on C acts on these conditional density operators even if the original input is an entangled state.

Fidelity of quantum states (F(ρ,σ))

Words: 297 Articles: 6
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
In the unsquared convention, quantum fidelity is F(ρ,σ)=Trρ​σρ​​. It equals the minimum classical Bhattacharyya coefficient over all POVMs.

Pure-state trace distance and fidelity identity (D=1−F2​)

Words: 37
Fidelity of quantum states OurBigBook.com
For pure states ρ=∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣ and σ=∣φ⟩⟨φ∣, the unsquared quantum fidelity is F=∣⟨ψ∣φ⟩∣. In their two-dimensional span, ρ−σ has trace zero and determinant −(1−F2), hence eigenvalues ±1−F2​. Its trace norm is twice the positive eigenvalue, giving trace distance D=1−F2​.

Unitary invariance of trace distance and fidelity

Words: 44
Fidelity of quantum states OurBigBook.com
For any unitary U, the unique positive square root of an operator obeys UAU†​=UA​U†. Conjugating the positive operators appearing in trace distance and quantum fidelity therefore conjugates their square roots. Cyclicity of the trace removes the unitary factors, proving invariance of both quantities under simultaneous unitary transformations of the states.
// Target: quantum-information-theory.bigb

Squared quantum fidelity (Fsq​(ρ,σ)=(Trρ​σρ​​)2)

Words: 56
Fidelity of quantum states OurBigBook.com
This is the square of the unsquared quantum fidelity, another common convention for fidelity. If one state is ∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣, it equals ⟨ψ∣σ∣ψ⟩. For two pure states it equals ∣⟨ψ∣φ⟩∣2. The ensemble average used in pure-state quantum source coding is normally the average of this overlap probability; the convention must be stated when comparing fidelity formulas.

Joint concavity of quantum fidelity (F(∑x​px​ρx​,∑x​px​σx​)≥∑x​px​F(ρx​,σx​))

Words: 39
Fidelity of quantum states OurBigBook.com
In the unsquared convention, F(∑x​px​ρx​,∑x​px​σx​)≥∑x​px​F(ρx​,σx​). Use Uhlmann's theorem to choose component purifications with nonnegative maximizing overlaps, and then construct matching flagged purifications of a quantum ensemble. Their overlap is the weighted sum on the right; the fidelity of the mixtures maximizes over all such overlaps.

Monotonicity of quantum fidelity under partial trace (F(TrB​ρ,TrB​σ)≥F(ρ,σ))

Words: 46
Fidelity of quantum states OurBigBook.com
Discarding a subsystem cannot decrease unsquared quantum fidelity: F(ρA​,σA​)≥F(ρAB​,σAB​). Maximizing purifications of the joint states are also candidates for purifications of the marginals, with the discarded subsystem included in the reference. Uhlmann's theorem then proves the inequality. Information loss makes the two states at least as similar.

Pure-state gentle measurement bound

Words: 56
Fidelity of quantum states OurBigBook.com
If M is a positive contraction and p=⟨ψ∣M2∣ψ⟩>0, the normalized successful post-measurement state is M∣ψ⟩/p​. Since M2≤M,
F(∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣,pM∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣M​)2=p⟨ψ∣M∣ψ⟩2​≥p.
(8)
A likely outcome therefore preserves a pure input well in quantum fidelity when its measurement operator is positive. Positivity excludes a hidden unitary rotation that could otherwise change the state even for an outcome of probability one.

Coherent information (Ic​(Λ,ρ))

Words: 196 Articles: 5
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
For a channel output Q and complementary environment output E, coherent information is Ic​(Λ,ρ)=S(Q)−S(E)=−H(R∣Q) for a purification reference R.

Mutual information and coherent information identity (I(R:B)=S(ρ)+Ic​(Λ,ρ))

Words: 31
Coherent information OurBigBook.com
For a purified input with reference R and channel output B, I(R:B)=S(R)+S(B)−S(RB)=S(ρ)+Ic​(Λ,ρ). The reference entropy is fixed through subsequent channels. Thus data-processing inequality for coherent information immediately implies data processing for quantum mutual information between that reference and successive outputs.

Coherent information upper bound by input entropy (Ic​(Λ,ρ)=S(ρ)−I(R:E)≤S(ρ))

Words: 32
Coherent information OurBigBook.com
In a purified Stinespring dilation, coherent information satisfies Ic​=S(RE)−S(E)=S(ρ)−I(R:E). Nonnegativity of quantum mutual information implies Ic​≤S(ρ). Equality means that the reference and environment are uncorrelated, so the environment learns nothing about the purified input reference.

Coherent information as an environment conditional entropy (Ic​(Λ,ρ)=S(R∣E)=−S(R∣B))

Words: 47
Coherent information OurBigBook.com
Purify the input on RA and dilate a channel by A→BE. The joint state RBE is pure, so complementary entropies obey S(B)=S(RE) and S(RB)=S(E). Therefore coherent information is Ic​=S(B)−S(RB)=S(R∣E)=−S(R∣B). The positive environment conditional entropy and negative receiving-system conditional entropy are two equivalent forms.

Data-processing inequality for coherent information (I(A⟩B)−I(A⟩B′)=I(A:E∣B′)≥0)

Words: 32
Coherent information OurBigBook.com
A quantum channel on the receiving system cannot increase coherent information: I(A⟩B)ρ​≥I(A⟩B′)σ​. Dilate the channel to a linear isometry of Hilbert spaces B→B′E. The difference is I(A:E∣B′) of the dilated state, nonnegative by Strong subadditivity of Von Neumann entropy.

Anti-degradable quantum channel

Words: 33
Coherent information OurBigBook.com
A quantum channel is anti-degradable when its receiver output can be simulated from the complementary environment output. Data processing then forces every coherent information to be nonpositive, and no-cloning prevents perfect quantum transmission.

Joint convexity of quantum relative entropy

Words: 20
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
Quantum relative entropy obeys D(∑i​pi​ρi​∥∑i​pi​σi​)≤∑i​pi​D(ρi​∥σi​). It follows by applying data processing to flagged block-diagonal states and discarding the flag.

Quantum ancilla

Words: 59 Articles: 1
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum ancilla is an auxiliary quantum system introduced to assist a state preparation, measurement, or channel use. Applying a channel to one part of an entangled system can reveal behavior invisible to inputs without an ancilla.

Ancilla qubit

Words: 22
Quantum ancilla OurBigBook.com
An ancilla qubit is a two-dimensional quantum ancilla. It is the quantum version of an ancilla bit; an auxiliary quantum register can contain several such qubits.

Quantum channel OurBigBook.com
A memoryless quantum channel has independent identical noise on successive uses, described by the tensor-power map Φ⊗n. This factorization does not restrict the encoder to product inputs: one can feed an entangled state across uses. A block code with equally likely messages m chooses states ρm​ and a decoder POVM (Dm​). Its average error is 1−∣M∣−1∑m​Tr[Dm​Φ⊗n(ρm​)], and its rate is n−1log2​∣M∣. The classical capacity of a quantum channel allows such entangled block inputs; the one-use Holevo capacity gives the product-input capacity and requires regularization in general.

A quantum erasure channel transmits an input state unchanged with probability 1−p and replaces it by an orthogonal, recognizable erasure flag with probability p. The entanglement-assisted classical capacity is consequently 2(1−p)log2​D bits per use; for a binary input it is 2(1−p).

Take independent ensembles for two quantum channels and their Cartesian product ensemble. A Lindblad dissipator is the non-Hamiltonian generator associated with a Lindblad operator V. It preserves the trace because cyclicity gives Tr(VρV†)=Tr(V†Vρ), cancelling the two anticommutator terms. It preserves Hermiticity and satisfies D[V](I)=[V,V†]; it need not preserve the identity or the purity of a density operator.
Lindblad operator
Words: 24
Lindblad equation OurBigBook.com
The Lindblad operators Lα​ describe dissipative channels in a Markovian open-system evolution. Their normalization fixes the corresponding rates, and their representation is not unique.
Lindbladian
Words: 160 Articles: 3
Lindblad equation OurBigBook.com
The Lindbladian L is the linear superoperator on density operators defined by the right-hand side of a Lindblad equation, so that ρ˙​=L(ρ).
Finite-dimensional Lindbladians have stationary states (∃ρ∗​: L(ρ∗​)=0)
Words: 53
Lindbladian OurBigBook.com
For any initial density operator, average its time-independent Lindblad equation trajectory as ρˉ​T​=T−1∫0T​ρ(t)dt. These averages stay in the compact convex set of density operators. Along a convergent subsequence, L(ρˉ​T​)=(ρ(T)−ρ(0))/T→0, so the limit is stationary. Thus a finite-dimensional physical Affine Bloch equation has at least one physical equilibrium, even though an arbitrary affine real equation can have none.
Lindbladian gap
Words: 29
Lindbladian OurBigBook.com
The Lindbladian gap is the smallest positive decay rate −Reλ among nonzero eigenvalues λ of a relaxing Lindbladian. It controls the slowest asymptotic exponential approach to the stationary state.
Unique stationary state of a Lindbladian
Words: 54
Lindbladian OurBigBook.com
A finite-dimensional Lindbladian converges to one stationary state for every initial state exactly when zero is a simple eigenvalue and every other eigenvalue has strictly negative real part. A trivial commutant of the Hamiltonian and all jump operators and their adjoints is a standard irreducibility criterion leading to uniqueness under the usual finite-dimensional hypotheses.
Quantum Trajectory Theory
Words: 91 Articles: 1
Lindblad equation OurBigBook.com
A quantum-trajectory unravelling represents a Lindblad equation as an ensemble of stochastic pure-state histories. In one jump unravelling, a state evolves between jumps under the non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian Heff​=H−2i​∑α​Lα†​Lα​, while a jump of type α sends it to a normalized multiple of Lα​∣ψ⟩.
Dark state of a Lindblad equation
Words: 44
Quantum Trajectory Theory OurBigBook.com
A pure stationary state is dark when every jump operator acts on it as a scalar, after an allowed shift of the jump operators, and the corresponding effective Hamiltonian preserves its ray. Every trajectory that reaches such a state remains on that same ray.

Quantum de Finetti theorem

Words: 81 Articles: 1
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
The quantum de Finetti theorem represents every infinitely exchangeable quantum state as a mixture of independent identically distributed product states. Finite versions approximate a fixed-size marginal of an N-exchangeable state by such a mixture with error tending to zero as N grows.

Mean-field ansatz from the quantum de Finetti theorem

Words: 38
Quantum de Finetti theorem OurBigBook.com
For a permutation-symmetric many-body problem with diverging coordination, finite-site reduced states approach mixtures of product states. Minimizing a local energy therefore reduces asymptotically to minimizing it over one-site density matrices, with separate one-site states allowed for distinct sublattices.

Separable quantum state

Words: 434 Articles: 12
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
A bipartite state is separable when it is a convex combination ∑j​pj​ρjA​⊗ρjB​ of product states; otherwise it is entangled.

Separable positive operator (ηAB​)

Words: 36
Separable quantum state OurBigBook.com
A separable positive operator is a finite sum ηAB​=∑y​αy​⊗βy​ with both factors positive operators. If its trace is one, normalizing the nonzero factors gives a separable quantum state. Conversely, a nonnegative scalar multiple of a separable quantum state is a separable positive operator.

Positive-map separability criterion

Words: 42
Separable quantum state OurBigBook.com
A finite-dimensional bipartite density operator ρAB​ is a separable quantum state exactly when (idA​⊗Φ)(ρAB​)≥0 for every positive linear map from operators on B to operators on A. In combination with the Størmer-Woronowicz decomposability theorem, it makes the positive partial transpose criterion sufficient for qubit-qutrit states. The criterion is established in the Horodeckis' separability paper.

Entanglement witness

Words: 21
Separable quantum state OurBigBook.com
An entanglement witness is a Hermitian operator W such that Tr(Wρ)≥0 for every separable quantum state ρ, but Tr(Wσ)<0 for at least one entangled state σ.

Partial transpose (ρTB​)

Words: 183 Articles: 4
Separable quantum state OurBigBook.com
In a fixed product basis, the partial transpose on subsystem B sends
∣i⟩⟨j∣⊗∣k⟩⟨ℓ∣⟼∣i⟩⟨j∣⊗∣ℓ⟩⟨k∣.
(19)
It preserves Hermiticity and trace but need not preserve positivity on entangled inputs.

Partial transpose of a maximally entangled projector ((∣Φd​⟩⟨Φd​∣)TB​=S/d)

Words: 27
Partial transpose OurBigBook.com
For ∣Φd​⟩=d−1/2∑j​∣jj⟩, the partial transpose of its pure state projector is S/d, where S is the swap operator. Expand in matrix units: ∣i⟩⟨j∣⊗∣i⟩⟨j∣ becomes ∣i⟩⟨j∣⊗∣j⟩⟨i∣.

Positive partial transpose (PPT)

Words: 84 Articles: 1
Partial transpose OurBigBook.com
A bipartite density operator has positive partial transpose when ρTB​≥0. Every separable quantum state has this property, since transposing one factor of a positive product state preserves positivity and the separable sum preserves it as well. The property does not depend on which local basis defines the transpose.
PPT maximally entangled overlap bound (F(∣Φd​⟩⟨Φd​∣,σ)≤d−1/2)
Words: 42
Positive partial transpose OurBigBook.com
Every density operator σ with positive partial transpose has squared quantum fidelity at most 1/d with a fixed maximally entangled state on d⊗d. The partial transpose of a maximally entangled projector and the trace-adjoint identity for partial transpose express that squared overlap as Tr(SσTB​)/d. Since σTB​ is positive of trace one and the swap operator has operator norm one, trace duality gives the bound. A matching product state attains equality.

Trace-adjoint identity for partial transpose

Words: 41
Partial transpose OurBigBook.com
For bipartite operators X,Y in a fixed product basis,
Tr(XYTB​)=Tr(XTB​Y).
(20)
Expand both operators in products of matrix units. On the transposed factor, the identity is Tr(AT)=Tr(ATTT); bilinearity gives the bipartite result. It allows a negative partial transpose eigenvector to define an entanglement witness.

Positive partial transpose criterion (PPT criterion)

Words: 19
Separable quantum state OurBigBook.com
Every separable state has positive partial transpose. The condition is also sufficient for separability on 2⊗2 and 2⊗3 systems.

Entanglement-breaking channel

Words: 114 Articles: 2
Separable quantum state OurBigBook.com
A channel is entanglement breaking when applying it to one side of every bipartite state always produces a separable state. Equivalently, its Choi matrix is separable, and equivalently it has a measure-and-prepare representation.

Separable Choi-state criterion for entanglement breaking

Words: 41
Entanglement-breaking channel OurBigBook.com
A quantum channel is entanglement breaking exactly when its Choi state is a separable quantum state. If CΛ​=∑a​pa​σa​⊗τa​, the Choi reconstruction formula gives a measure-and-prepare channel with POVM Ea​=dpa​τaT​. Conversely, applying an entanglement-breaking channel to a maximally entangled state produces a separable Choi state. Horodecki, Shor and Ruskai's entanglement-breaking channel paper develops the equivalences.

Rank-one Kraus representation of an entanglement-breaking channel

Words: 40
Entanglement-breaking channel OurBigBook.com
An entanglement-breaking channel admits a Kraus representation with rank-one Kraus operators Kj​=∣aj​⟩⟨bj​∣. Its Choi state is a sum of positive tensor-product operators, hence separable. Conversely, spectral decompositions of each prepared state and each POVM effect in a measure-and-prepare channel produce rank-one Kraus operators. Trace preservation imposes ∑j​∥aj​∥2∣bj​⟩⟨bj​∣=I.

Isotropic quantum state

Words: 50
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
For two d-dimensional systems, an isotropic quantum state has the form
ρp​=p∣Φ+⟩⟨Φ+∣+(1−p)d2I​,
(21)
where ∣Φ+⟩=d−1/2∑j​∣jj⟩ is a maximally entangled state. This parametrization is separable exactly when p≤1/(d+1).
The defining symmetry is U⊗U invariance. This differs from the U⊗U invariance of a Werner state; members above the displayed threshold are entangled.

Swap operator (F)

Words: 29
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
The swap operator exchanges two tensor factors: F(∣ψ⟩⊗∣ϕ⟩)=∣ϕ⟩⊗∣ψ⟩. It has eigenvalue +1 on the symmetric subspace and −1 on the antisymmetric subspace, and the partial transpose of ∣Φ+⟩⟨Φ+∣ is F/d.

Pretty good measurement (PGM)

Words: 19
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
For ensemble {pj​,ρj​} with average ρˉ​=∑j​pj​ρj​, the pretty good measurement has Mj​=ρˉ​−1/2pj​ρj​ρˉ​−1/2 on the support of ρˉ​.

Quantum state discrimination

Words: 19
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
Quantum state discrimination uses a measurement in quantum mechanics to identify which candidate density operator was prepared. Minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination impose different objectives; quantum binary hypothesis testing is the two-state case.

Quantum binary hypothesis testing

Words: 241 Articles: 5
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
Quantum binary hypothesis testing chooses a two-outcome measurement to distinguish two candidate density operators, trading the probabilities of the two kinds of error.

Binary test for quantum decoding success (F0​=∑m​∣m⟩⟨m∣⊗Em​)

Words: 58
Quantum binary hypothesis testing OurBigBook.com
For k equiprobable quantum code states decoded by a POVM {Em​}, testing whether the classical message label agrees with the decoded output gives a joint binary POVM with F0​=∑m​∣m⟩⟨m∣⊗Em​. Its acceptance probability is the decoding success 1−ϵ on the joint classical-quantum state and 1/k on the product of its marginals. Applying quantum relative entropy monotonicity to this test gives the one-shot classical-quantum coding converse.

Quantum channel discrimination

Words: 66 Articles: 1
Quantum binary hypothesis testing OurBigBook.com
Quantum channel discrimination feeds a common input into one of several candidate quantum channels and measures the output. An entangled quantum ancilla permits inputs ρHR​ and compares (Tj​⊗idR​)(ρHR​); optimal binary discrimination is governed by the diamond norm of the weighted channel difference.

Diamond norm of the transposition map

Words: 29
Quantum channel discrimination OurBigBook.com
For the transposition map Θ:Md​→Md​, the induced trace norm is ∥Θ∥1​=1, while stabilization gives
∥Θ∥⋄​=d.
(22)
Thus an entangled quantum ancilla can amplify the distinguishability witnessed by transposition by a factor of d.

Holevo–Helstrom theorem

Words: 94 Articles: 1
Quantum binary hypothesis testing OurBigBook.com
For hypotheses ρ0​,ρ1​ with priors p,1−p, the optimal success probability is
Psucc∗​=21​(1+∥pρ0​−(1−p)ρ1​∥1​).
(23)
An optimal measurement projects onto the positive and negative spectral subspaces of the weighted difference.
This is the minimum-error optimum in binary quantum state discrimination.

Equal-prior discrimination of qubit states (psucc​=21​+41​∣r−s∣)

Words: 57
Holevo–Helstrom theorem OurBigBook.com
For equiprobable qubit states with Bloch vectors r,s, their density-matrix difference is (r−s)⋅σ/2, with eigenvalues ±∣r−s∣/2. An effect 0≤E≤I declaring the first state yields success 1/2+Tr[E(ρr​−ρs​)]/2. Selecting its positive-eigenvalue eigenspace maximizes this trace and proves the displayed result. Measure along r−s and attach the corresponding state labels; if the vectors coincide, no measurement improves on guessing.

Entanglement monogamy

Words: 93 Articles: 3
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
Entanglement monogamy limits how strongly one subsystem can be entangled with several independent partners.

Coffman--Kundu--Wootters inequality (CA:BC2​≥CAB2​+CAC2​)

Words: 33
Entanglement monogamy OurBigBook.com
For a pure state of three qubits, the squared concurrence obeys CA:BC2​≥CAB2​+CAC2​. In particular, if A and B form a maximally entangled pair, then A has no entanglement with C.

Entanglement area law

Words: 46 Articles: 1
Entanglement monogamy OurBigBook.com
An entanglement area law bounds the entropy of a region by a constant times the size of its boundary.

Tensor-network area-law bound

Words: 27
Entanglement area law OurBigBook.com
If a bipartition cuts n∂​ tensor-network bonds of dimension at most χ, its Schmidt rank is at most χn∂​ and its entanglement entropy is at most n∂​logχ.

Werner state

Words: 25
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
A Werner state is a bipartite density operator invariant under U⊗U for every local unitary operator U. An isotropic quantum state instead has invariance under U⊗U; these are different families.

Ancilla bit

Words: 25
Quantum information theory OurBigBook.com
An ancilla bit is an auxiliary bit providing workspace in reversible computation. In a quantum circuit, an ancilla qubit provides quantum workspace; a general quantum ancilla need not be a single bit.
